locators.chapter_or_section: Chapter 5 — The Kernel of Good Strategy
locators.claim_scope: Diagnosis, guiding policy and coherent action are connected components of the strategy kernel.
Strategy quality requires identifying a challenge rather than substituting goals, vague language or inconsistent objectives.
Objectives should be feasible and reduce ambiguity in light of organizational capabilities.
Interdependent activities can reinforce strength or constrain isolated improvements.
Strategy as hypothesis and execution as a source of proprietary functional knowledge.

locators.claim_scope: Price and value discussions belong early in product development.
Segmentation should reflect customer needs, value and willingness to pay.
Offer configuration should reflect the segment rather than simply contain every feature.
How a business charges is a distinct design choice from the price point.
External willingness-to-pay evidence should inform an evolving business case.
Consider nonprice explanations and alternatives before reflexive discounting.

locators.chapter_or_section: Step 1 — Customers Who Love Your Product
locators.claim_scope: Positioning needs sufficient customer evidence to reveal a useful pattern.
Understand alternatives from the customer perspective, including manual and status-quo choices.
Comparative capabilities require evidence; consideration and retention attributes can differ.
Relate capabilities to benefits and customer goals.
Value relevance differs by customer and situation.
A market frame should make relevant strengths understandable and requires customer context.
A trend can support positioning but should not replace a clear market context.
Positioning should be shared with sufficient detail for cross-functional use.
Translate positioning into sales and messaging, and review changes through customer perceptions.
